newsitem.title: CHINA: China oil exports to Japan seen steady until 2000.
newsitem.headline: China oil exports to Japan seen steady until 2000.

text.p: China will maintain its contracted oil exports to Japan until the year 2000 but shipments afterwards may fall as domestic demand rises, senior officials from state trading firm Chinaoil said on Friday.
"China is expected to maintain the current arrangement until 2000 but exports would be subject to price and further negotiations," a senior official said.
The official, who asked not to be named, said this was the conclusion of senior government officials.
"Exports after the year 2000 would be reviewed again," said another senior Chinaoil official.
Chinaoil, a joint venture between state trader Sinochem and onshore oil producer China National Petroleum Corp (CNPC) is reponsible for crude oil exports from China.
China has been exporting between six and eight million tonnes of crude oil to Japan a year under the contract.
The export price, published monthly, is linked to the price of a mixture of Indonesian crudes.

A senior official from CNPC told Reuters earlier that China's crude output from its two main oilfields - Daqing and Shengli- was not expected to rise significantly in the near term but domestic demand was climbing sharply.
China's Daqing oilfield produces about 50 million tonnes of crude every year and Shengli about 30 million tonnes per year.
